en: The amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool, dry air to the Philippines between November and February.
The habagat, or southwest monsoon, causes heavy rains and flooding in western parts of the Philippines.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is a perfect cone stratovolcano that frequently erupts due to tectonic subduction.
The town of Pugad in Bulacan is famous for mining and carving white marble into sculptures.
The Bicol region has highly fertile volcanic soil enriched by past eruptions of Mount Mayon.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features a navigable underground waterway that flows directly into the sea.
Filipino farmers traditionally look for the Balatik constellation, part of Orion, to signal the dry planting season.
The gravitational pull of the moon creates high and low tides affecting daily fishing in Manila Bay.
The Philippine Trench is a deep oceanic fault where tectonic plates collide, frequently causing strong earthquakes.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of thousands of limestone mounds formed from ancient coral reefs.
PAGASA uses local Filipino names to track typhoons that cross the Philippine Area of Responsibility.
Surigao del Norte contains massive nickel laterite deposits that are mined for stainless steel production.
